title: EVA-RADIUS – Evaluation of an interactive cross-sectoral blended treatment approach for alcohol use disorders after withdrawal
summary:
The study is interested in enabling people with an alcohol addiction to receive seamless follow-up treatment after withdrawal treatment. To this end, an online therapy program was developed that helps to maintain contact with the therapist while reducing personal therapy contacts. The aim of the study is to find out whether this program, called RADIUS, is just as effective as more frequent and longer face-to-face contacts.
The planned study should provide information on whether the so-called RADIUS program is just as effective as conventional treatment. Both programs are based on the so-called CRA approach (Community Reinforcement Approach). Behavioral therapy combined with a so-called community-oriented positive reinforcement approach, i.e. in addition to a precise analysis of personal patterns of behavior and conduct, possibilities for change in everyday life are worked out. The success of the therapies is measured by the number of days without alcohol, which we ask about before the therapy, for the duration of the therapy, for the three months afterwards and a further six months later.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of alcohol: Dependence syndrome

interventions.name: In the first study arm (3 sessions of CRA + RADIUS; intervention condition), participants receive 3 sessions of CRA lasting 30 minutes within 3 months and also have access to the RADIUS online tool during the treatment period.
In the control condition study arm (CRA; control condition), the subjects receive 6 sessions of outpatient face-to-face therapy of 50 minutes each according to the CRA approach within 3 months.
In the third study arm (6 sessions of CRA + RADIUS; comparison group), instead of the 3 sessions, the participants receive 6 sessions of CRA lasting 50 minutes within 3 months and the RADIUS tool.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Current moderate (4-5 symptoms) or severe (>6 symptoms) alcohol use disorder (F10.2 according to DSM-5 and alcohol dependence according to ICD-10 F10.2). The criteria for alcohol dependence according to ICD-10 are also currently fulfilled (F10.2)
-	Participants must be undergoing withdrawal treatment at the time of inclusion 
-	have a sufficient command of written and spoken German
-	be 18 to 65 years old
Exclusion criteria:
-	Acquired brain damage/brain trauma, CNS-relevant somatic diseases (e.g. multiple sclerosis, epilepsy), serious somatic diseases requiring acute treatment
-	Current life-threatening crises with suicidal tendencies
-	self-harming behavior
-	Psychotic disorder (current or in the last year),  
-	Eating disorder with body mass index < 15
-	Substance dependence on centrally active substances other than alcohol and nicotine
